title: muP learning-rate transfer at char-LM scale: hand-rolled muP cuts the optimal-LR drift 3.1x (SP -1.19 -> muP -0.38 octaves per width doubling) and the zero-shot transfer penalty 21.6x (0.578 -> 0.027 bpc at 4x width), and muP's own coordinate check confirms the mechanism (last-block activation-update RMS grows 6.01x with width under SP, 1.25x under muP) - but the optimum is NOT width-invariant: muP still loses a full octave from d=32 to d=64 and only stops drifting once both models are >= 64 wide, localizing the failure to a base width too narrow to be asymptotic rather than to muP itself
hypothesis: Under muP (Yang & Hu, Tensor Programs V, arXiv:2203.03466) the loss-optimal base learning rate of a nanoGPT-style char LM is width-invariant, so it can be tuned on a narrow proxy and transferred; under standard parametrization (SP) it drifts toward smaller LR as width grows. Measured as the shift of argmin_lr in octaves per width doubling.
question: At 0.03-0.42M params and 500 steps - three orders of magnitude below where muTransfer has been validated - (a) does the SP optimal LR actually drift, and by how much per width doubling; (b) does a correctly hand-rolled muP make it stand still, or merely slow it down; (c) what does the practitioner actually pay for transferring the proxy-tuned LR, in bits per character; and (d) does muP's own coordinate check agree with whatever the loss curves say?
method: HAND-ROLLED muP; microsoft/mup is NOT installed. base_width n0 = 32, width multiplier m = d_model/n0 in {1,2,4}. Rules follow TP5 Table 3 (abc-parametrization, muP column, Adam rows) and Table 8 (width-multiplier form, the form the mup package ships) plus the 1/d attention rule of TP5 Sec.4/Table 8. IMPLEMENTED TABLE - input/embedding: std sigma0 (0.02), Adam lr eta, mult 1, IDENTICAL in both arms; hidden matrices (qkv/proj/fc/out): std 1/sqrt(fan_in) in both arms, Adam lr eta (SP) vs eta/m (muP); readout d->V: SP std 1/sqrt(d) + mult 1 + lr eta, muP std 1/sqrt(n0) + mult 1/m + lr eta; LayerNorm gains/biases: lr eta in both; attention logits: q.k/sqrt(d_head) (SP) vs q.k*sqrt(d_head0)/d_head (muP). TWO DOCUMENTED DEVIATIONS FROM A NAIVE READING, BOTH DELIBERATE: (1) the readout row is TP5's 'output weights' row (mult 1/fan_in, init var 1/fan_in^2, Adam lr 1/fan_in) put through the abc-symmetry of TP5 Sec.3.3 -- (mult,std,lr) -> (mult/theta, theta*std, theta*lr) leaves Adam training exactly invariant because Adam's per-entry step is scale-free -- with theta = m, giving the (mult 1/m, width-independent init, width-independent lr) form the mup package actually ships (MuReadout applies output_mult/width_mult in the forward pass; MuAdam classifies the readout as vector-like, one finite dim, and leaves its LR alone). This is the one row practitioner tables disagree on; the Theta(1)-logit-update condition pins it: Delta(mult*W*h) ~ mult*lr*d*h_rms = (1/m)*eta*(m*n0)*h_rms = Theta(1) requires lr = Theta(1) GIVEN mult = 1/m. (2) the attention rule is written sqrt(d_head0)/d_head rather than bare 1/d_head; the constant is the mup package's tunable attn_mult (its README literally uses `query @ key.T * 8 / d`, 8 = sqrt(64) for base head dim 64), fixed to the value that makes muP coincide with SP at the base width -- standard base-width HP alignment, without which the arms would already differ at m=1 by a constant. CONSEQUENCE AND MAIN CONTROL: at d=32=base_width SP and muP are the SAME parametrization, so their curves must coincide exactly; run.py measures this (base_width_identity_max_abs_bpc_diff) and gets EXACTLY 0.0 across all 7 LRs, which is what licenses attributing the entire d=64/d=128 gap to width scaling. SWEEP: 2-layer pre-norm decoder-only char LM, n_head = 2 HELD FIXED so width scaling grows head_dim 16->32->64 (the case where the 1/d_head rule bites), d_ff = 4d, ctx 64, tiny-shakespeare 65 chars, 90/10 split. 7 base LRs at integer octaves 2^-11..2^-5 x widths {32,64,128} x {SP,muP} = 42 runs, 500 steps, batch 16, 1 seed. Pure Adam (weight_decay 0: decoupled WD interacts with muP and is a separate question), 20-step linear warmup then CONSTANT lr (sharper minima than cosine), grad clip 1.0. Every run gets the identical seeded init draw and the identical batch stream -> tightly paired. ARGMIN is reported both as the discrete grid point and as the vertex of the parabola through the grid minimum and its two neighbours (sub-octave resolution); drift is the OLS slope of argmin log2(lr) against log2(width), i.e. octaves per width doubling. TRANSFER PENALTY: take the grid-optimal LR at the base width, apply it zero-shot at each larger width, subtract that width's own tuned optimum. CURVE GAP: mean |dbpc| between the d=64 and d=128 curves over all 7 LRs, i.e. does the WHOLE curve transfer or just its argmin. COORDINATE CHECK (muP's own diagnostic, run separately at fixed lr 2^-7): RMS change of every residual-stream site and of the logits over 6 Adam steps on a fixed probe batch, at all 3 widths in both arms. Deterministic, CPU-only, 1 torch thread.
architecture: nanoGPT-style pre-norm decoder-only transformer, 2 layers, 2 heads (fixed), d_ff = 4d, ctx 64, no biases in linear layers, LayerNorm, GELU; d_model in {32, 64, 128} = 31,104 / 111,360 / 419,328 params; two parametrizations (SP and hand-rolled muP) differing only in per-layer Adam LR scaling, readout multiplier + init, and attention logit scale

dataset.name: tiny-shakespeare, character level, 65-symbol vocab (1,003,854 train chars / 111,540 val chars)

task: next-character prediction; headline = the location of the minimum of the val-bits-per-character vs base-learning-rate curve as a function of width, under SP vs muP. This is a SHAPE experiment (where the minimum sits), NOT a quality experiment: 500 steps at 0.03-0.42M params leaves every model far from converged and absolute bpc is not the point.
framework: torch 2.13.0 (CPU, single thread), numpy, matplotlib; muP hand-rolled from TP5 Table 3/Table 8 (microsoft/mup NOT installed)
compute: CPU 1 thread, 795.2 s (13.3 min) total: 42 trainings of 500 steps (784.9 s of training+eval; ~8-9 s per d=32 run, ~13-14 s per d=64, ~28 s per d=128, with some contention from co-running agents) + 6 coordinate checks (~10 s)

metrics.headline: argmin base-lr drift: SP -1.19 octaves per width doubling, muP -0.38 (3.1x less); argmin spread over d=32..128: SP 2.38 oct, muP 0.95 oct; zero-shot transfer penalty at d=128 from an LR tuned at base width 32: SP +0.578 bpc vs muP +0.027 bpc (21.6x less)
metrics.base_width_identity_note: SP and muP are the SAME parametrization at m=1 by construction; measured difference is exactly 0.0 at all 7 LRs, so the entire d=64/d=128 gap is attributable to width scaling

mup_drift_is_all_in_the_first_doubling.note: muP's residual drift is ENTIRELY the 32->64 step; between the two widest models transfer is effectively exact

metrics.quality_verdict: muP is NOT a quality win here: best bpc at d=128 is SP 3.016 vs muP 3.023 (tie); at d=64 muP 3.043 vs SP 3.144. muP buys tunability, not loss.
metrics.coord_check_note: 6 Adam steps at fixed lr 2^-7 on a fixed probe batch; muP's intended vanishing init logits (1/sqrt(m) decay) and width-flat update sizes both appear, independently validating the hand-rolled implementation before any loss curve is read

result_summary: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED - muP wins the practical question decisively and loses the literal one. (1) SP DRIFTS, AS ADVERTISED: the argmin base LR moves from 2^-7.04 at d=32 to 2^-9.03 at d=64 to 2^-9.42 at d=128, an OLS slope of -1.19 octaves per width doubling and a 2.38-octave spread over a 4x width range, close to the textbook 1/width story. (2) muP CUTS THAT 3.1x BUT DOES NOT STOP IT: 2^-7.04 / 2^-7.99 / 2^-7.80, slope -0.38 oct per doubling, spread 0.95 oct. All 6 minima are interior on the 2^-11..2^-5 grid and 0 of 42 runs diverged, so no argmin is a boundary artifact. (3) THE PRACTITIONER'S NUMBER IS THE LOPSIDED ONE: tune the LR on the d=32 proxy (2^-7) and apply it zero-shot at d=128 and SP costs +0.578 bpc against that width's own optimum while muP costs +0.027 - a 21.6x difference, and the SP number is enormous in absolute terms (comparable to the entire spread of results in most of this lab's architecture ablations). It is not just the minimum that transfers under muP either: the mean |dbpc| between the d=64 and d=128 curves across all 7 LRs is 0.204 under SP and 0.049 under muP, a 4.2x tighter agreement of the whole curve, and the SP curve sharpens with width (depth 0.394 -> 0.534 -> 1.132 bpc) while muP's stays flat (0.394 -> 0.493 -> 0.485), so under SP a mis-transferred LR is both more likely and punished harder. (4) THE COORDINATE CHECK VALIDATES THE IMPLEMENTATION INDEPENDENTLY OF THE LOSS: over 6 Adam steps at fixed LR the RMS change of the last block's activations grows 6.01x across a 4x width increase under SP (3.91 -> 9.30 -> 23.48, i.e. roughly linear in width - exactly the instability muP exists to remove) but only 1.25x under muP (3.91 -> 4.49 -> 4.87); logit updates grow 1.46x under SP and 0.93x under muP; and muP's intended vanishing init logits appear as 1.03 -> 0.65 -> 0.48 (~1/sqrt(m)) against SP's flat 1.03 -> 0.93 -> 0.98. This is muP's own diagnostic agreeing with the loss curves, and it is what rules out a mis-implemented readout LR (the one rule where practitioner tables disagree: a factor-m error there would have made muP's logit-update RMS decay like 1/m, and it does not). (5) THE HONEST NEGATIVE, AND WHERE IT LOCALIZES: muP's residual -0.38 oct/doubling is not noise-shaped - it is ENTIRELY the 32->64 step (-0.95 oct), while 64->128 moves +0.19 oct, i.e. transfer between the two widest models is effectively exact. That is the signature of a base width too narrow to be asymptotic rather than of muP failing: the Cerebras/EleutherAI practitioner guide picks a proxy hidden size of 256 'to ensure a large-enough scale for the law of large numbers and central limit theorem to converge' and d=32 (head_dim 16) is 8x below that. With 1 seed and a 1-octave grid this experiment cannot separate that explanation from ordinary curvature and does not claim to. (6) muP IS NOT A QUALITY WIN: best bpc at d=128 is SP 3.016 vs muP 3.023, a tie (at d=64, muP 3.043 vs SP 3.144). muP buys tunability, not loss - which is exactly what it advertises. CAVEATS: 1 seed; 500 steps leaves every model far from converged so this measures the shape of an early-training LR landscape, not a converged one; weight decay is set to 0 and the muP/AdamW interaction is untested; n_head is held fixed so only head_dim scales; the SP<->muP diff bundles three changes (hidden-LR downscaling, readout multiplier+init, attention scale) and is not decomposed, which matters because arXiv:2605.21486 argues nearly all of muP's AdamW benefit is the relative embedding LR alone.

novelty_check.conclusion: REPLICATION at a new (much smaller) scale, with two measurements the prior art does not report. The claim itself is canonical: TP5 (2203.03466) states and proves it, microsoft/mup implements it, and the EleutherAI/Cerebras Practitioner's Guide publishes the exact SP-drifts-vs-muP-aligned figure this row reproduces. The definitive empirical study, 'A Large-Scale Exploration of mu-Transfer' (2404.05728), was fetched directly and confirms two things that position this row: it sweeps widths 128/512/2048/8192 and DOES NOT TEST WIDTHS BELOW 128, and it finds SP's 1/sqrt(d) attention scale alone prevents transfer. The Practitioner's Guide fetch confirms it neither publishes its smallest width nor quantifies the drift, and recommends a proxy hidden size of 256 - the number that explains this row's residual. WHAT THIS ROW ADDS: (a) it runs an octave BELOW the smallest published mu-Transfer width (32 vs 128) and finds the regime where muP only partially transfers, with the failure localized by width-step to the narrowest model (all of the -0.95 oct is 32->64; 64->128 is +0.19 oct); (b) it reports the drift as a SCALAR (octaves per width doubling, with sub-octave parabolic argmin interpolation) and as a zero-shot TRANSFER PENALTY IN BPC (SP 0.578 vs muP 0.027), rather than as a figure to eyeball, plus a whole-curve agreement metric (0.204 vs 0.049); (c) it adds a BASE-WIDTH IDENTITY CONTROL - SP and muP are constructed to be the same parametrization at m=1 and measure as exactly 0.0 apart - which none of the fetched treatments report and which is what licenses attributing the entire gap to width. It does NOT decompose the muP diff into its three parts, which arXiv:2605.21486 (2026) argues is where the real story is. The 'not published at this scale' claim rests on 4 web searches and 3 direct fetches, not an exhaustive review.
